annotation.title_clean: Drones and new systems of warfare – the EU's need to adapt to be fit for today's security challenges
annotation.title_en: Drones and new systems of warfare – the EU's need to adapt to be fit for today's security challenges
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union (C series)
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament resolution of 22 January 2026 on military and counter-drone systems. It calls for scaling EU drone and C-UAS production, supply-chain autonomy from China, EU-NATO-Ukraine cooperation, harmonised certification and interoperability standards, a binding EU regulatory framework for military drones, and human-in-the-loop control over lethal autonomous systems.
key_provisions_or_claims: Calls on the Commission to propose an EU Drones Package, including a regulation on civilian and military drone use
Calls for a binding EU framework for military drone operations covering rules of engagement, certification, airspace and ethical safeguards
Requires development of autonomous drones to be governed by international humanitarian law and a human-in-the-loop principle (para 180)
Calls for EU-origin criteria, a Drone Sovereignty Index and onshoring of critical components to cut dependence on China
Calls for a drone wall, an EU-NATO interoperability standard, joint testing hubs and harmonised pilot and operator certification
